headline: Jubo League leader dies in custody a day after arrest in Chattogram
summary: Nurul Alam, a joint convenor of the Dhemsha Union Jubo League, died at Chattogram Central Jail after doctors reported a massive heart attack.
details: Nurul Alam, a Jubo League leader from Satkania, died at Chattogram Central Jail on Wednesday morning. He had been arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of police on Tuesday afternoon.

According to Senior Jail Superintendent Iqbal Hossain, Nurul complained of chest pain and difficulty breathing on Wednesday morning. He was rushed to Chittagong Medical College Hospital, where he was declared dead.
Doctors initially stated that Nurul had suffered a massive heart attack. The authorities have stated that the body will be handed over to the family following an autopsy.
Nurul's elder brother, Nur Mohammad, has alleged that his brother was 'murdered' and demanded a fair investigation. He claims Nurul was arrested due to a land dispute with local residents.
The family further alleges that Nurul was healthy when he entered the prison on Tuesday evening and that he had not been active in politics for some time.
Efforts to reach Chattogram District Additional Superintendent of Police (Detectives) Mohammad Ibrahim and Satkania Police chief Jahangir Alam for comment were unsuccessful.
caption:
A Jubo League leader died in Chattogram Central Jail just one day after his arrest. His family is now alleging murder.

Nurul Alam, a Jubo League leader from Satkania, died at Chattogram Central Jail on Wednesday morning. He had been arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of police on Tuesday afternoon.

According to Senior Jail Superintendent Iqbal Hossain, Nurul complained of chest pain and difficulty breathing on Wednesday morning. He was rushed to Chittagong Medical College Hospital, where he was declared dead.

Doctors initially stated that Nurul had suffered a massive heart attack. The authorities have stated that the body will be handed over to the family following an autopsy.

Nurul's elder brother, Nur Mohammad, has alleged that his brother was 'murdered' and demanded a fair investigation. He claims Nurul was arrested due to a land dispute with local residents.

The family further alleges that Nurul was healthy when he entered the prison on Tuesday evening and that he had not been active in politics for some time.

Efforts to reach Chattogram District Additional Superintendent of Police (Detectives) Mohammad Ibrahim and Satkania Police chief Jahangir Alam for comment were unsuccessful.

headline_marked: School exams rescheduled: [[Half-yearly exams to start July 1]]
headline: School exams rescheduled: Half-yearly exams to start July 1
summary: The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) has announced new dates for half-yearly and pre-test exams across all educational institutions.
details: The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) has revised the schedule for half-yearly and pre-test examinations for government and private educational institutions.
The new schedule applies to lower secondary, secondary, and school and college levels across the country.
According to an official order issued on Tuesday, June 23, 2026, the examinations will now begin on July 1 and conclude on July 16.
The exams were previously scheduled to start on June 28 and end on July 13, as per a notification from the Ministry of Education dated May 20.
The DSHE has directed all principals and headteachers of government and private institutions to implement these changes due to unavoidable reasons.
All educational institutions have been requested to follow the updated directive to ensure a smooth examination process.
caption:
Half-yearly and pre-test exams are moving! New dates announced for all schools and colleges.

The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) has revised the schedule for half-yearly and pre-test examinations for government and private educational institutions.

The new schedule applies to lower secondary, secondary, and school and college levels across the country.

According to an official order issued on Tuesday, June 23, 2026, the examinations will now begin on July 1 and conclude on July 16.

The exams were previously scheduled to start on June 28 and end on July 13, as per a notification from the Ministry of Education dated May 20.

The DSHE has directed all principals and headteachers of government and private institutions to implement these changes due to unavoidable reasons.

All educational institutions have been requested to follow the updated directive to ensure a smooth examination process.
